### class MaterialPropertyBehaviour : PlayableBehaviour — Timeline/MaterialPropertyBehaviour.cs:9
Runtime stand-in for one MaterialPropertyClip while the timeline plays. Only points at its pose; the mixer reads and blends.

### class MaterialPropertyClip : PlayableAsset, ITimelineClipAsset — Timeline/MaterialPropertyClip.cs:15
One pose on a MaterialPropertyTrack: the shader values it sets. A value the pose doesn't list keeps the material's own value. Saved in the timeline asset; never changed while playing.
- `ClipCaps clipCaps { get; }` :29 — undocumented
- `override double duration { get; }` :31 (override)
- `override Playable CreatePlayable(PlayableGraph graph, GameObject owner)` :33 (override)

### class MaterialPropertyMixer : PlayableBehaviour — Timeline/MaterialPropertyMixer.cs:14
Every frame: blends the active poses by their weights and writes the result into the bound image's material. Works on a private copy of the material (UI materials are shared) and puts the original back when the timeline stops.
- `override void ProcessFrame(Playable playable, FrameData info, object playerData)` :30 (override)
- `override void OnPlayableDestroy(Playable playable)` :65 (override)

### class MaterialPropertyTrack : TrackAsset — Timeline/MaterialPropertyTrack.cs:17
Timeline row that animates a UI image's material: its clips are poses (named shader values); overlapping clips crossfade. Optionally writes the Timeline's time into a shader property, so shader motion follows Speed x2 and scrubbing.
- `override Playable CreateTrackMixer(PlayableGraph graph, GameObject go, int inputCount)` :23 (override)

### class InputIcon : MonoBehaviour — InputIcon.cs:20
Shows one input action's button for the device the player uses (LastUsedDevice), drawn by the InputGlyphs package; if a fill is given, the button fills left to right while held (Hold). Knows nothing about who shows it or when: its parent turns it on and off. Needs the InputGlyphsSetup prefab once in the scene.

### class LastUsedDevice — LastUsedDevice.cs:14
Knows which device the player used last (keyboard, mouse, gamepad), so on-screen prompts can show that device's buttons. Shared and static like the Input System itself; mirrors device state only, never game state. Starts by itself, read-only from outside.
- `static InputDevice Current { get; }` :21 — The device used last; null if none is connected.
- `static event Action Changed` :25 — Raised when Current changes; read Current again.

Makes a body's authored walk fit how it really moves and the ground under it. Reads only how the body moved since last frame (Walker, a script, a teleport) and drives the Animator: Speed blends stand into walk, WalkRate plays the walk at the pace the body travels, so the feet don't slide. Then fits the feet to the ground the way action games do (a trace per foot, the foot offset by the ground's height, the body lowered to the lower foot, all smoothed), with one difference: our legs are soft bendy tubes, not two bones, so a leg reaches a nearer foot by bowing more and a farther one by straightening, solved directly each frame (no iterations, so no jitter). A planted foot is locked where it stands, whatever the body does (foot locking); a lifting foot plans its landing so the whole foot lands on flat ground (stride fitting). When the walk isn't stepping, as when the body turns on the spot, feet left behind step back under it on their own, one at a time.

### class Walker : MonoBehaviour — Walker.cs:15
Takes its body to a destination over the NavMesh at a calm pace: turns towards where it goes, slows down before arriving, optionally turns to a final facing, then reports Arrived. Moves only the body's transform; legs are WalkMotion's job, which reads the motion.
- `event Action Arrived` :38 — Raised once the body stands at the destination, facing as asked.
- `bool IsWalking { get; }` :40 — undocumented
- `void WalkTo(Vector3 destination, Quaternion? finalFacing = null)` :54 — Starts walking; replaces any walk in progress. Throws if the NavMesh has no path there.
- `void Stop()` :70 — Stops where it is, without Arrived.

## Oyung.SharedKernel

### class Condition — Condition.cs:13
Shared Kernel contract: a question about some module's state ("is the intro seen?", "has 3 flowers?"). Knows nothing itself; each state owner subclasses it in its own .Unity side to ask about its own data. Used by deciders (Story, NPC AI), which hold it inline and never know which module answers.
- `abstract bool IsMet { get; }` :17 — True when the condition holds right now. Cheap, no side effects. Throws if the provider isn't bound.
- `abstract event Action Changed` :24 — Raised when a value the condition reads has changed; ask IsMet again. The answer itself may stay the same. Subscribe with a method, not a lambda, so you can unsubscribe (-=) when you stop caring.

### interface ICataloguedItem — ICataloguedItem.cs:9
Shared Kernel contract: an asset a catalog holds and finds by its stable name; saves and dialogue use the same name. Unique within its catalog.
Implemented by: ActorId (Oyung.Actors), IGlobalFact (Oyung.Globals), ModuleFact<T> (Oyung.SharedKernel.Unity)
- `string Name { get; }` :11 — undocumented

### interface ISaveBlocker — ISaveBlocker.cs:9
Shared Kernel contract: lets any module say "saving is not possible right now" without knowing the save module. Named locks: saving is allowed only while no reason is held, and one module's Unblock never cancels another's Block.
Implemented by: SaveSystem (Oyung.Save)
- `void Block(string reason)` :13 — Holds a block under this reason, e.g. "cutscene". The same reason may be held more than once.
- `void Unblock(string reason)` :17 — Releases one block held under this reason. Throws if none is held: an unbalanced pair is a bug.

### interface ISaveable — ISaveable.cs:12
Shared Kernel contract: a module that keeps state across saves. A section is a dictionary of plain values: bool, int, long, float, double, string, a nested section, or a list of those. Anything else (an enum: write its name) throws on save. Numbers come back wider than they went in: whole numbers as long, decimals as double.
Implemented by: ActorStore (Oyung.Actors), CutsceneStore (Oyung.Cutscenes), GlobalStore (Oyung.Globals), QuestJournal (Oyung.Quests), SaveSystemTests.FakeSaveable (Oyung.Save.Tests), SequenceStore (Oyung.Sequences)
- `string Section { get; }` :15 — The section's stable name in the save.
- `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object> Give()` :18 — The module's current state.
- `void Take(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object> section)` :23 — Puts back what Give returned, silently: runs in the load phase, before anything listens. Not called if the save has no such section; the module then simply starts fresh.

### class Instruction — Instruction.cs:13
Shared Kernel contract: an order to change some module's state ("set intro_seen", "remove 5 flowers"). Knows nothing itself; each state owner subclasses it in its own .Unity side. Used by deciders (Story, NPC AI), which hold it inline and never know which module carries it out.
- `abstract void Execute()` :18 — Carries out the order. Strict: if it can't be done (precondition broken), throws naming the asset. To check first, the designer pairs it with a Condition.

### class StringInstruction — StringInstruction.cs:12
Shared Kernel contract: an order that carries a text only known while playing ("remember this name"). Like Instruction, each state owner subclasses it on its own .Unity side, and the decider holds it inline without knowing which module carries it out.
- `abstract void Execute(string value)` :16 — Carries out the order. Strict: throws naming the asset if it can't be done.
